title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In pp. 293–650 of the continuation of 'La Longue Marche', Grothendieck studies the 'équation des lacets' (loop equation). These are the relations that an outer automorphism of the profinite group π̂_{0,3} (the fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}) must satisfy when it comes from Galois with tangential basepoints. The data are an element α_0 (resp. f) and an exponent ν. The relations are written using:
- ρ, the order-3 symmetry permuting 0, 1, ∞;
- σ_∞, the complex-conjugation-type involution;
- l_0, the loop around 0.

This is the same circle of relations that Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara later codified as the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group. Here the parameter μ = 2ν+1 plays the role of λ = 2m+1 in GT.

On the previous page Grothendieck projects everything to the 'linear shadow' GL(2,Ẑ). There π̂_{0,3} maps to the closure of Γ(2), the free subgroup of index 12 in SL_2(Z). He showed that the validity of ξ = ε l_0^ν φ is equivalent to a cocycle-type identity g ρ(g) ρ²(g) = ±1, which he left in suspense.

This page takes the case h = 1 (the variant where the β_0-term is trivial).
- (47)–(49): write α_0 = (a b; c d) and f = (r s; t u) with entries in Ẑ, det α_0 = δ = ±1 and det f = 1.
- (50): ξ = α_0 ρ(α_0)^{-1}.
- (51): φ = f σ_∞(f)^{-1}. Here σ_∞ acts on SL_2 as inverse transpose, so σ_∞(f)^{-1} = ᵗf and φ = f ᵗf. This gives the symmetric matrix (53): R = r²+s², S = T = rt+su, U = t²+u².
- (52), quoted from §42 (78): δA = (a²+ab+b²) − (ac+bd+bc), δB = ac+bd+bc, δC = ac+bd+ad − (c²+cd+d²), δD = c²+cd+d².
- Verification of (52): it is exactly what one gets with ρ = conjugation by P = (0 −1; 1 −1), the order-3 element of SL_2(Z). One computes α P α^{-1} P^{-1} and multiplies by det α^{-1} = δ.
- (54) C + D − B = 1 follows, because δ(C+D−B) = ad − bc = δ. (55) S = T is the symmetry of φ.

The key equation is (56) ξ = ε l_0^ν φ, the 'relation des lacets' with ε = ±1, equivalently l_0^{-ν} ξ = ε φ. With l_0^{-1} = (1 2; 0 1) this becomes, on the next page, a matrix equation. Symmetry gives 2νD = C − B; with (54) this yields μD = 1, μ = 2ν+1, and then μU = ε and D = εU.

Marginal NB, the 'arithmetic' case coming from π̂_{0,3}·{1, σ_∞}: then α_0 ≡ f ≡ 1 mod 2, i.e. a, d, r, u odd and b, c, s, t even. This is because the image lies in the closure of Γ(2).

Purpose. Grothendieck is solving the loop equation at its first, linear (SL_2 / Γ(2)) level, in order to see which exponents ν are compatible. The outcome is that μ = 2ν+1 must be a unit, equal to 1/D — the cyclotomic-character constraint.
errors: (48) as written in the image reads 'ab − cd = δ'. This must be the determinant ad − bc = δ: (54) C+D−B = 1 follows from (52) precisely because δ(C+D−B) = ad − bc. It is a slip of the pen (or a misreading).
The transcription writes ρ_0^ν in (56); the manuscript has l_0^ν (the loop around 0), consistent with the previous and next pages.
The marginal note 'δ = ε_3' links the determinant sign to an earlier sign convention; it cannot be checked from this page alone.

ideas.what: Projecting the loop/hexagon-type relations for Galois automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} to the linear quotient via Γ(2) ⊂ SL_2, and solving them explicitly with matrices
ideas.modern_name: Image of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller relations (GT relations with λ = 2m+1) in GL_2(Ẑ); the 'linearized' or level-2 shadow of the Galois action on π̂_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld 1990 and Ihara 1991 for GT; Lochak–Schneps and others for its images and quotients
ideas.where_published: The program is announced in the Esquisse d'un programme (1984). These continuation pages of the Longue Marche (pp. 293–650) are not, as far as I know, published.

ideas.what: Explicit formula for the commutator-like map α ↦ α ρ(α)^{-1} with ρ = conjugation by the order-3 element (0 −1; 1 −1), and the identity C + D − B = 1
ideas.modern_name: Elementary matrix identity / coboundary for an order-3 automorphism

ideas.what: σ_∞ acting as inverse transpose, so that φ = f ᵗf is symmetric
ideas.modern_name: Complex conjugation as Cartan-type involution on SL_2

ideas.what: Mod-2 congruence condition in the arithmetic case (α_0 ≡ f ≡ 1 mod 2)
ideas.modern_name: Closure of Γ(2) as the image of π̂_{0,3} in SL_2(Ẑ)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly works with the loop equation, parametrised by ν with μ = 2ν+1, in matrix form in SL_2(Ẑ). This is a pre-Drinfeld manipulation of GT-type relations at the linear level. The next page derives μD = 1, i.e. μ is the inverse of a matrix entry and so a unit, matching λ = 2m+1 ∈ Ẑ^×. This documents that he was solving these equations concretely, not only announcing them.
missed.quote: La relation essentielle reliant α_0 et f ... est la relation ξ = ε l_0^ν φ , ε ∈ {±1} "relation des lacets"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historical record of the pre-1990 origin of GT-type relations. The mathematics on this page is elementary and the linear quotient of GT is understood today.

missed.claim: The SL_2(Ẑ) shadow considered here is implicitly the Galois action on the Tate module of the Legendre curve over P^1 − {0,1,∞}. In that reading, the constraint μD = 1 is the cyclotomic-determinant condition. The page does not state this link, and it is a natural but not new observation.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This reading is minor and likely known to specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out a routine matrix computation within an unpublished but known program: Grothendieck's anticipation of GT. Its interest is mainly historical, as a concrete working-out of the loop equation in SL_2(Ẑ); there is no new theorem.
transcription_corrections: (56) and the following line: 'ρ_0^ν' should read 'l_0^ν' (and 'l_0^{-ν} ξ = ε φ').
(48) reads 'ab − cd = δ' in the manuscript, but ad − bc is meant.

Top-right marginal note: the reading 'changements de signes dans α_0 ... immaterial' is uncertain. It seems to say something like 'changements de signes des lignes de α_0 immatériels', i.e. sign changes of α_0 are immaterial.
Left margin: '...arithmétique, i.e. qui provient de π̂_{0,3}, α_0 de π̂_{0,3} = π_{0,3}^∧·{1,σ_∞}, on aura α_0, f ≡ 1 (2), i.e. a, d, r, u ≡ 1 (2), b, c, s, t ≡ 0 (2)' — this is essentially correct.
